Lesson No. 215: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 1 to 3

The surah opens with this decisive statement.

﴿Tanzil al-Kitab min Allah al-Aziz al-Hakim﴾ (39:1) "The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise." He is Mighty, and He has the power to send down a Book of this kind. And He is Wise: He knows what the revelation of the Qur'an is about and why it is wise. All of these affairs Allah carries out with perfect wisdom, deliberation and decree.

The discussion of this statement is not lengthy, because it serves as an introduction (tamhid) to the main matter and the central theme, to which this entire surah is devoted. The very descent of the surah is itself the proof and reinforcement of this theme: namely, the doctrine of tawhid (Divine Oneness), tawhid in the worship of Allah, and tawhid in the Islamic system of life. It also means purifying belief, worship and the system of life from shirk in every aspect, and then, by removing intermediaries, calling upon Allah directly, without any intercession, to reach Him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verse 2:

"Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth" (39:2). "O Prophet ﷺ, We have sent down this Book to you in truth." And the truth upon which it has been sent down is comprehensive Oneness (tawhid), upon which this entire universe is established. In the fifth verse of this surah it says:

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾ (39:5). "He created the heavens and the earth with truth." Therefore, the truth upon which the heavens are established is the same truth that is the subject of this Book. The concept of tawhid in this Book and the unity of the creation of this universe are one and the same. Just as this universe is the creation and handiwork of the One God, and just as this human being is established by God's creation and His command, so too this Book is established upon God's command. Therefore, the logical result is:

﴿So worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ (39:2). "So worship Allah, making your religion pure for Him alone."

The address is to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to whom this Book was sent down in truth. And this Book is the way of life presented by the Messenger, to which he invites all of humanity. It rests upon the belief that Allah is One, that He alone is to be worshipped, that the system of life is to be derived from Him alone, and that the entire life is to be established upon this belief in Tawhid.

To regard Allah as the one God and to make religion pure for Him is not merely a matter of a few words uttered by the tongue. In reality, it is a complete system of life, which begins in the heart and mind of a person with the belief in Tawhid and culminates in the establishment of a complete system of life in an Islamic society.

The heart that regards Allah alone as its God, that worships Allah alone, does not bow its head before anyone. It neither asks anything from other than Allah, nor relies upon anyone other than Allah. For such a person, only Allah is mighty, and only Allah is dominant over this entire universe. He prevails over all. All others are weak and feeble, and none of them has the power to benefit or harm anyone. Therefore, a human being should not bow his head before another human being, because all of these humans are just like him, and they are not even the masters of their own benefit and harm. Allah alone is the Giver and the Withholder. Therefore, Allah has no need of any intermediary or means in this matter. All creation is in need of Him, and He is free of need.

Furthermore, the heart that is filled with the belief in Tawhid also believes that one and the same law of nature and order of creation governs this universe. Therefore, it believes that the system of life that Allah has prescribed for humanity is also a part of those laws of nature which have been established for this universe. Therefore, such a human being cannot live in harmony with this world unless he adopts the Islamic system of life. Hence he adopts those commands and arrangements which Allah desires, that is, he obeys the Shari'ah of Allah, which is in harmony with the system of this universe and the system of human existence.

Furthermore, the heart that considers Him to be One without partner perceives a closeness and connection between itself and the entire creation of this Allah, whether living or lifeless. Therefore, its life is spent in an environment that is its friend, sympathizer and helper, and that walks alongside it and loves it. It perceives in its environment the workings of Allah's power. Therefore, it lives in that environment in intimacy with Allah and His creatures. The creatures of Allah are with it. Its eyes are upon the wonders created by Allah. It does not harm anything in this universe here. It does not destroy anything in this universe except by the command of Allah, because Allah alone is the Creator of everything. He alone gives life. He is the Lord of all and the Lord of everything.

In the same way, Tawhid manifests itself in human life in thoughts and inclinations. Tawhid also has an effect on human conduct and demeanour. And Tawhid has an effect on the methodology and way of life for human life and society. The belief in Tawhid does not remain merely a word that is uttered with the tongue. It becomes a complete system. This is the reason why in the entire Qur'an the belief in Tawhid has been given immense importance. Everywhere it has been emphasized and repeated. Therefore, Tawhid must be contemplated from these perspectives. From this perspective, Tawhid becomes a thought, a collective system and a system of government. And it requires constant reflection upon it. In every age, in every family and society, and in this very sense, there is a need to reflect upon it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verse 3:

﴿Surely, to Allah belongs sincere religion (al-din al-khalis).﴾ (39:3) In a very high, very long and very awe-inspiring voice, as though it were a royal proclamation. The word "Ala" (Alā, "Beware!") opens it, and it is expressed in the most emphatic words of restriction and exclusivity: that the right to rule over life belongs to Allah alone, and sincere religion is the right of Allah alone. Just as the meaning is emphasised, so the words are majestic. This is a principle of life. The whole of life stands upon it, and indeed the whole of the universe stands upon this proclamation. This is why this law is enforced in such brief, powerful words of restriction and exclusivity. And consider what the slogan and doctrine of the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) of that time was, which was rejected.

﴿As for those who take protectors besides Him, [saying], "We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in closeness." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.﴾ (39:4) They used to proclaim that Allah is their Creator, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. But then they walked along the path of natural reasoning: if He is the Creator, then He alone is worthy of worship, and then religion, law and legislation should be His alone. At this point they would invent the fable that the angels are the daughters of Allah. Then they would make images of the angels and worship them. They would then say that they worship the idols of the angels, whom they called gods: Lat, Manat and Uzza. In truth, they were not worshipping them, but merely bowing before them so that these angels might intercede for them with Allah, and thus they would become close to Allah.

This belief is a deviation from straightforward natural thinking, and along with being false, it is also complicated and incomprehensible. The angels are not the daughters of Allah, nor are these idols the idols of the angels. Allah has not permitted it. Allah does not hear anyone's intercession, and Allah does not bring His servant near to Himself by this method.

Whenever humanity has abandoned the belief in Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah), it has been deprived of the straightforward manner of thinking and simple reasoning of nature, which Islam brought from the very first day, and from Adam (peace be upon him) until now all the noble messengers presented this same belief in Tawhid. We see that today, in the same way, righteous people and saints are worshipped, just as in the time of the Prophet ﷺ the Arabs worshipped the angels and the idols of the angels as a means of drawing near to Allah, according to their own assumption. The aim was to obtain their intercession. But Allah points to the belief in Tawhid and to the straight path: a Tawhid with which there is no confusion, no intercessor, and no legendary near ones of God.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and a disbeliever.﴾ (39:3) Because these people lie about Allah. One lie is that the angels are the daughters of Allah; the second lie is that they intercede with Allah on their behalf, whereas the angels themselves deny their being worshipped. These people in reality disbelieve the clear commands of Allah. Therefore Allah does not guide those who fabricate lies against Him and deny Him. Guidance is granted to those who are sincere, attentive, desirous of avoiding evil, interested in good deeds, and who reflect and choose the right path for themselves. Those who fabricate lies and deny the verses of Allah are not deserving of Allah's guidance and mercy, because such people knowingly take a path other than the right one. After this, the weakness and emptiness of this polytheistic conception of God is made manifest.

This is a hypothetical argument. The point is that if God wished to take a partner, He would choose one from among His creation and announce it. His will is unrestricted, but God's essence is free of such things. Therefore, a son cannot be attributed to God, nor is God the son of anyone. This is God's will, His decree, and His destiny. Far is God above these things.

﴿Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Irresistible.﴾ (39:4) Holy is He from such things; He is Allah, alone and dominant over all. When would Allah take anyone as a son for Himself? He is the Creator of everything, the Originator of everything, the Governor of everything. Everything and every person is in His possession, and He disposes of them as He wills.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verse 5:

Verse No. 5

A brief glance at the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, at the system of night and day, at the system of the sun and the moon, and at the sight of their being subjected in a mighty manner, establishes the proof that there is no deity except Allah. This natural order impresses upon the heart that Allah has neither a partner nor a son.

In the creation of the heavens and the earth, the proofs of Allah's oneness are entirely manifest, and in the laws that govern them too, the signs of the Divine oneness are apparent. A mere cursory glance at this whole universe makes clear that countless proofs exist. In the scientific discoveries that humans have made to date, there are countless proofs for the oneness of divinity. It has been established for humans that this universe, to the extent that humans have reached it, is made of particles whose reality and nature are one, and each of these particles is composed of rays whose reality is one. It is also known that the celestial bodies formed from these particles, whether they are the ones in which we live or other planets and stars, are all in complete motion, and this motion has a specific continuous law from which no star can deviate. The smaller particles and the stars share the same motion, and the greatest particles of this world also share the same motion. Then, the study of the universe also shows that this motion has a system. This system is the reality which provides evidence that the Creator and Manager of this entire universe is one. The new realities that scientists discover every day show that what is placed in the plan of this universe bears witness to the being of Allah alone, and is a truth, and does not change according to people's desires, nor does it incline in any direction according to the inclinations of any person. It does not abandon its path for a single second, nor does it adopt deviation.

"Khalaqa as-samawati wal-ard bil-haqq" (39:5): "He created the heavens and the earth with truth." And He also revealed the Book with truth. Therefore there is truth in this universe and there is truth in this Book, and it is one and the same truth which is in this universe and in this Book, and the source and origin of both is one and the same. Both are signs that the Creator of this universe is one.

"Yukawwirul-layla 'alan-nahari wa yukawwirun-nahara 'alal-layl" (39:5): "He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night." This mode of expression is such that it grasps a person by the hem and draws his attention to the modern discoveries according to which the earth has been proven to be round. Despite the desire that I keep myself away from modern scientific discoveries in the exegesis of the Holy Quran, because human theories are sometimes correct and sometimes wrong, today proven and tomorrow falsified, whereas the Quran is the truth and is itself its own proof of its truthfulness, "Aftab amad dalil-e-aftab" (the sun has come, the proof of the sun). The Quran does not seek proof of its truth from its supporters or opponents, nor from those discoveries which this weak human provides. Yet despite this attitude, this mode of expression compels me to reflect on the rotation of the earth on its axis and its spherical structure, because a visible scene is clearly seen through this expression, and its denial is not possible. The earth is round, and with its axial rotation it faces the sun. Therefore the part of it which faces the sun is lit and is day, but this part does not remain in one place. As soon as this part moves forward, darkness covers that part of the earth and wraps it. Thus the part of day is being wrapped and the night wraps it. From the other side, where the night is wrapped, it too advances, and light wraps the part of night, and day comes in it. Thus on one side the night covers (Cover) the day, and on the other side the night covers the day, and this motion continues.

"Yukawwiru-l-layla 'ala-n-nahari wa yukawwiru-n-nahara 'ala-l-layl" (39:5): These words draw an excellent picture of the situation, and the correct picture of the situation enters the mind. In this way the nature of the earth's motion is also expressed, the roundness of the earth is also established, and its orbit is also established. This is the best exegesis of this mode of expression; no other exegesis can be deeper than this.

"Wa sakhkharash-shamsa wal-qamara kullun yajri li-ajalin musamma" (39:5): "He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running until an appointed term." The sun is moving in its orbit and the moon is moving in its orbit, and both are subjected by the command of Allah. No one claims that he is driving them, and natural reasoning does not accept that this motion takes place without any mover, and that this extremely intricate system runs with such regularity that after many millions of years we see not the slightest decrease in this motion. These sun and moon will continue in this manner and will continue for a set time, that is, until the Day of Resurrection, and knowledge of it belongs to none but Allah. When the command comes, they will stop.

"Alaa huwal-'Azizul-Ghaffar" (39:5): "Be aware, He is the Mighty, the Forgiving." Therefore, by virtue of power, might and dominance, He sustains the universe, and along with this power He is also Ghaffar. He forgives the shortcomings of those who turn towards Him, even though they had committed great crimes such as denial and shirk. They used to make deities alongside Allah, then they assign offspring to Allah and commit other crimes, but the door of repentance is open, the path for entering through it is clear, and Allah is the Mighty and the Forgiving.

After this brief glance at the study of this great universe, the address now turns briefly to the very small self of man, who holds within himself a great world, focusing only on this aspect: reflect a little upon "life" and "existence."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verse 6:

Verse No. 6

When a human being reflects upon his own self, upon that self which he did not create, and whose origin he does not himself know, he possesses only that knowledge which Allah, the Creator, has given him. The human self is one; its essence is one. Its characteristics are one, and some of the characteristics of this human self are entirely distinct from those of other creatures. Just as all the individuals of the human self are limited and distinguished within a specific sphere, so too the "human self" is one among the billions of individuals who are scattered across or dwell upon this earth. From this single self, its mate or spouse was also created. In all human characteristics, woman shares with man. Although the detailed characteristics differ, the fundamental characteristics are one and the same. This shows that the structure of man and woman is according to one and the same blueprint. Within that same blueprint, through certain modifications, man and woman became distinct from one another. It is one and the same will that distinguishes man from woman.

In reference to and in connection with the differences between man and woman within the human self, a hint has also been given here to the systems of male and female in the important species of other animals, so that it may be understood that in this entire universe, and among animals other than humans as well, the truth is operative.

"Wa anzala lakum minal-an'ami thamaniyata azwaj" (39:6): "And He sent down for you eight pairs of livestock." These eight animals, male and female, as they are mentioned in other verses, are sheep, goats, cattle and camels. That is, counting male and female, they make eight. And when the males and females are collectively considered, the word "azwaj," meaning pairs, is applied to them, and thus a whole is formed.

The manner of expression indicates that Allah has sent them down, that is, created them and made them subservient for you. This subjugation is a decree from Allah. It is an accomplishment of Allah's exalted majesty, and Allah has permitted that humans may use the flesh of these eight kinds of animals. After mention of the characteristics of male and female among animals, a reference is then made to the various stages of the embryo found in the wombs of mothers.

"Yakhluqukum fi butuni ummahatikum khalqan min ba'di khalqin" (39:6): "He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation." First the sperm drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then a clear form, and finally the creation within it of human faculties and the creation of human characteristics.

"Fi zulumatin thalath" (39:6): "In three veils of darkness." First, the darkness of the sac in which the embryo is, the darkness of the womb in which it is wrapped, and then the mother's belly in which the womb is situated. The hand of Allah's power continually causes this particle to grow day by day, and this hand of power keeps increasing it day after day. Then its shape and form keep changing, and it keeps advancing. Allah watches over this creature and gives it the power to grow, and thus it becomes possible for its form to change. It advances step by step, according to Allah's decree and measure.

When one considers this brief journey of human beings and reflects closely upon these far-reaching transformations of their structure, it becomes evident that through the wondrous characteristics within it, and under their guidance, this weakest and microscopic cell developed in the manner it did, amid those darknesses and in that marvelous way. Thus a person becomes certain that all these matters lie beyond human knowledge, insight and power.

All these realities are sufficient to compel human beings to recognize the Creator of the universe. A person should come to know the Creator of the universe through these living signs, and the unity (wahdaniyyah) present within this creation is manifest. Its signs are entirely clear and apparent, and how can any thinking person disregard them?

"Dhalikum Allahu rabbukum, lahu al-mulku, la ilaha illa huwa, fa-anna tusrafun" (39:6): "That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. There is no deity but He. So how are you being turned away?"

Beholding these signs of the one Allah, and observing these marks of Allah's unrestrained power, people are here made to stand up and reflect upon their own conduct, and it is told to them that now before them there are only two paths: the path of gratitude and the path of disbelief. Whichever path you adopt, the full consequences of it rest upon you individually. And a hint is given that the time is near, and this stage of the world is about to end. Then there will be reckoning and accounting, and this reckoning will be taken by the Being who brought you out of three darkest veils and made you responsible. And He already knows the most hidden matters of your hearts.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 39, verse 7:

Verse No. 7

The period of your mothers' wombs is only a brief part of your long journey of life. It is the initial stage. Then, once you come out of the womb, you will enter a comparatively long stage. After that will come the third, long and everlasting stage: the reckoning and accounting. And this stage will be carried out under the management of Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware.

As for the Being of Allah, He does not need a weak creature like man. Man is an extremely weak creature. It is the grace and bounty of Allah that He turns His attention towards human beings, watches over them and shows mercy to them, and how weak and how feeble they are.

﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need from you﴾ (39:7). Because your faith cannot add anything to the dominion of Allah, and your disbelief cannot decrease anything from it. But Allah does not approve of disbelief from His servants, and He does not love disbelief.

﴿And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ (39:7). And if you are grateful:

﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ (39:7). He loves gratitude, and rewards it with good.

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ (39:7). In the end, we shall return to Allah. We shall be presented only before Him, and there is no refuge other than Him.

﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ (39:7). Nothing is hidden from Him.

﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ (39:7). This is the end of life. These are the proofs of guidance, and this is the crossroads where the two paths diverge: one path of guidance and one path of misguidance. Now every person has the choice of which path he takes. Whoever takes a path should take it with full understanding, after reflection and contemplation, with knowledge and thought.

Lesson No. 216: At a Glance

The first lesson stated the story of human creation: that you were created from a single soul, and from that same soul a pair was made. Then cattle were created in countless pairs. Then you were given creation after creation within your mothers' wombs, and you were created in three darknesses. Then Allah bestowed upon you human characteristics, and then established the continuity of these characteristics and developed them.

Now the psychological condition of human beings is described: what their state is at times of joy, grief, safety and fear. How weak they are, how changeable of temperament, and how feeble and powerless they are, unless they establish a connection with the Lord, keep their hope fixed upon Him, become obedient to His commands, recognize the right path, attain the real truth, and set themselves on the course of those human characteristics which Allah has given to man.

Lesson No. 216: Explanation of the Verses

Verse No. 8

It is the nature of man that when dangers befall him, his human nature comes fully to the surface, and all the veils and coverings that lie over that nature are removed, and all illusions and superstitions are also dispelled. At a time of danger, a person turns only to the Lord, the Majestic, and bows before Him. At that time the human nature perceives that this danger can be averted only by Allah's removing it. All other powers prove false besides Allah.

But when difficulties are lifted, and a period of peace, security and prosperity arrives, and Allah replaces hardships with blessings, and thus difficulties are removed, this same person whose nature had come fully to the surface then becomes entangled in illusions and superstitions and falls under the influence of his former condition. He forgets his entreaties in hardship, his turning to Allah, and his repentance.

At that point he is no longer in a state where he calls upon Allah, fears Him, and believes that none other than Allah can remove difficulties. Forgetting all these circumstances, he once again associates others with Allah. Either he worships those gods which were worshipped in the age of ignorance, or he worships certain individuals. He serves circumstances that become partners with Allah, just as every jahiliyyah (state of ignorance) has its own deity. Sometimes he worships his own desires and his own interests, or he fears the hopes of the future and the unknown dangers, or he worships his children and his progeny, or he worships his chiefs and leaders. Remember that these chiefs too are worshipped just as God is worshipped; sometimes they are worshipped even more than God. Remember also that there are many kinds of shirk. Some forms of shirk are extremely subtle: people neither see them nor are they aware of them. The Qur'an does not take only well-known and apparent shirk, but takes everything that, in its own form, amounts to shirk.

The result is that such a person is led astray from the path of Allah, because the path of Allah is one; in it there is no possibility of plurality. That path means that life belongs only to Allah, love is for Allah alone, and no partner of Allah exists even in a person's thought. Neither the god of wealth should be a partner, nor the god of progeny, nor the god of homeland, nor the god of land, nor the god of kinship. Whichever form of shirk settles in someone's heart, it becomes a part of that deviation. There is misguidance from the path of Allah, and the end of misguidance from the path of Allah is the Fire, and this matter will soon come before him after the brief life of this world.

﴿Say: Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; surely you are among the companions of the Fire﴾ (39:8). However long the days of this world may be, they are still few. Man's days upon the earth are in any case limited, even if a person attains a long life. Indeed, the life of the entire human species on this earth is brief. When we compare this lifespan with the Days of Allah...

In contrast to this evil picture, there is also a good picture and a good psychological state: a heart that fears Allah, that remembers Allah in every condition and in every calamity, that lives in this world keeping the Hereafter in view, that seeks the mercy of Allah, that maintains such a connection with Allah that correct knowledge is born from it, and that attains the reality of this universe. Its picture is this:

Verse 9

This is an extremely vivid and sensitive picture. To be obedient and submissive, to be in a state of prostration and in a state of bowing, is in reality a sensitive submissiveness. Such a person fears the Hereafter and hopes for the mercy of Allah. This purity and this clarity of the inner self opens up human insight and grants the human heart and mind the power to see, to grasp, and to reflect. Through all these matters a very fine picture of the believers is drawn. Whereas in the previous verse there was a most unsightly picture of the polytheists. Now observe the comparison between them.

﴿Say: Are those who know and those who do not know equal?﴾ (39:9)

True knowledge is in reality the name of divine recognition. It is the name of reaching the truth. And such knowledge opens up human insight, and thus a scholar gains access to those realities which exist in this existence. Knowledge is not the name of information that gathers in the mind without any true principle or true reality being firmly established in the intellect, nor a reality that sits in the mind other than the perceptible.

This is the right path: real knowledge, and the truth which illuminates the heart and mind. This is what it means to be obedient to Allah: a sensitive heart, hope in the Hereafter and in the grace and bounty of Allah, and this is the fear of Allah, to remain frightened and awed before Allah. Knowledge, and true knowledge, is this, and thus rationality is produced; it is a faculty that sees, hears, and benefits from what it finds, and thus this kind of knowledge reaches, behind these observations, the supreme Reality. But those who call individual experiences knowledge, and who call only those things information which are visible, such people are collectors of information, but they are not scholars.

﴿Only those of understanding remember.﴾ (39:9) That is, those of open hearts, whose doors of insight can peer behind the outward appearances and observable phenomena. Those are the people of intellect, and they are the ones who, seeing the signs of Allah in everything, do not forget the certainty of accountability before Allah. After these two pictures, the believers are addressed: that they should fear Allah, do good deeds, and in this brief life send ahead something for the long life, having earned and prepared it.

Verse 10

Say: O My servants who have believed, (qul yā ʿibādi alladhīna āmanū) (39:10). This is a most gracious regard for the believers. In the original Arabic the wording is:

Qul yā ʿibād alladhīna āmanū (39:10), meaning: convey to them this message of mine, that they become God-fearing and fear their Lord. But Allah has changed it into the form of direct address. This is a kind of proclamation and warning. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not address the Muslims as "Yā ʿibādī" (O My servants); he would call them "ʿIbād Allāh" (servants of Allah). But it is Allah's gracious regard that He tells the Messenger (ﷺ) to call them "Yā ʿibād." Thus this call comes from Allah, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) relates Allah's direct address.

Qul yā ʿibādi alladhīna āmanū ittaqū rabbakum (39:10): "O Prophet, say: O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord." Taqwa is what? It is the sensitivity of the heart: looking towards Allah with fear and awe, looking with hope and longing, and remaining wary of His wrath and displeasure. This is the best conception of the people of faith. The imagery drawn in this verse and the colours filled in are the same as in the preceding verse, except that these are practical colours.

Lilladhīna aḥsanū fī hādhihi al-dunyā ḥasanah (39:10): "For those who did good in this world, there is good." What an excellent reward: do good in this world, and you will find goodness here in this lowly world and also goodness in the Hereafter, which is the abode of permanence and everlastingness. This is grace and bounty upon man, and Allah knows how weak and frail man is; therefore Allah has shown him boundless mercy.

Wa-arḍu Allāhi wāsiʿah (39:10): "The earth of Allah is spacious." Therefore, let not love of the land and attachment to any single place carry you away. Ties of lineage, kinship and friendship should not hold you back from great undertakings. Migration (hijrah) is for a great purpose. If some place is constricted for your religion, and where you cannot establish the beneficent system of Islam, then clinging to the land is the work of Satan, and it is a shade of shirk in the heart of man.

This is a most subtle indication of the Qur'an: it penetrates so covertly into the mind and heart of man that the matter being discussed is the oneness of Allah and fear of Allah, and yet this subtle indication is made within it. From this it becomes evident that the source of the Qur'an is that same Divine Being who created mankind, because the cure for the heart and mind of man can only be provided by the One who is the Creator of man and who has complete knowledge concerning man, and knows the hidden recesses of human personality.

Allah knows how very difficult this migration is for human beings. To abandon these worldly ties all at once is no easy matter. To leave a functioning life, the sources of sustenance to which a person has become accustomed, to abandon a going concern, and to begin life afresh in an entirely new land is a very difficult task. Man prepares for it only with difficulty. This is why this matter is called great patience here, and a great and full reward is promised for it.

Innamā yuwaffā al-ṣābirūna ajrahum bi-ghayri ḥisāb (39:10): "Those who are patient will be given their reward without reckoning." Here Allah addresses human hearts with a most fitting sense of this, and encourages them toward a task that is generally very arduous for people. Holy is He who is Forbearing and All-Aware regarding man, who deals with human hearts with such tenderness, and who knows the most hidden feelings lying in the depths of the ups and downs of human psychology, and provides their remedy.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verse 15:

Verse No. 15

Once again the declaration is made: "Behold, I walk upon my own path. I worship none but Allah, and I adopt as my system of life none but Allah's. As for you, follow whatever path you like and worship whomever you wish. But you will suffer this great bankruptcy. You will incur such a great loss that no loss will be greater than it. You will bring your own soul to Hell. You will suffer the loss of your families, whether they are believers or disbelievers. If they are believers, they will go to the Gardens while you will be in Hell, and they will certainly be fewer than you. If they are disbelievers, then just as you lost yourselves, so you also lost them. Both will be in Hell."

﴿Verily, that is the manifest loss﴾ (39:15). "And here is a scene of that loss":

This is a dreadful scene. It is a scene of fire. Above them there will be layers of fire, and beneath them too, and they will be enveloped by these canopies, and these flames, which have been called canopies, will overwhelm them. Allah presents this dreadful scene to His servants while they are still in the world, and if they wish to avoid it, they can avoid it.

﴿Dhalika yukhawwifu Allahu bihi ʿibadahu﴾ (39:16) "This is the end with which Allah frightens His servants." He calls out to them loudly: beware, beware! Ahead lies a great danger.

﴿Ya ʿibadi fattaqun﴾ (39:16) "O My servants, fear Me, [and beware of] My wrath." And on the other side, on the opposing platform, stand those who have been saved, who in the world feared this evil end:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verses 17–18:

Verses 17 to 18

The word ṭāghūt (the one who transgresses all bounds; false deity or tyrant) derives from ṭughyān. Like malakūt, ʿaẓamūt and raḥmūt, its form carries the sense of massiveness and exaggeration. Its commonly understood meaning is: whoever rebels and goes beyond all limits is a ṭāghūt. And who are those who avoid the worship and obedience of ṭāghūt? They do not worship ṭāghūt in any form. These will be the people who worship Allah in every matter, great and small, who turn to Him, who return to Him, and who stand at the correct station of servitude.

For such people there is good news from the higher realm, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is conveying this glad tidings to them.

﴿لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَىٰ ۚ فَبَشِّرْ عِبَادِ﴾ (39:17) "For them is good news. So give good news to My servants."

Good news came to them from the higher realm, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conveyed it. What greater blessing could there be? A characteristic of such servants of Allah is that when they hear a word of Allah, they listen to it attentively. Then they follow it, because it is the best, and they leave aside other words. Therefore they accept only what is good. Through it they purify their minds and hearts. It is always the case that pure and good souls are always open to pure and good words; they accept them immediately, while impure and wicked hearts are closed to good things and accept only filthy words.

﴿أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَاهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ (39:18) "These are the ones whom Allah has guided."

Because Allah saw that goodness existed in their hearts, He guided them to goodness, and they heard good words and accepted them. Guidance is indeed Allah's guidance.

﴿وَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمْ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ (39:18) "And these are the people of understanding."

Sound reason itself inclines people towards purity and towards salvation. Therefore whoever does not incline towards purity and salvation is, in effect, deprived of reason, and has rejected the blessing Allah has given. Before presenting the end and outcome of the pure people, it is said that these servants of ṭāghūt have in fact already reached the Fire in practice, and not one of them can escape the Fire.

Verse 20

The lofty buildings prepared for those who fear Allah, that is, the upper chambers, stand in contrast to the scene of the people of Hell, over whom there will be canopies of fire above them and canopies below them. Lesson No. 218: At a Glance

This lesson offers a glimpse into the world of plants: how Allah sends down water from the heavens, how the earth becomes green and produces crops, and how these crops reach their completion. In the Qur'an this image is given to show the impermanence of the earth and the brevity of the life of this world, and people of reflection and insight are directed to ponder it. Alongside the descent of water from the heavens, it is also shown that this Book is itself a kind of rain of mercy that descends from the heavens, and through it hearts that were dry become green and open. At this point a highly suggestive picture is also presented of how open hearts benefit from this Book. They fear it, a trembling comes upon them, their skins shiver, and softened, they become receptive, and then, having accepted guidance, they become deeply tranquil. Then comes the picture of those who respond to the remembrance of Allah, and the picture of those whose hearts have become like stone. At the end, the reality of tawhid is alluded to, and an example is given of the condition of those who worship the One God and of those who worship many deities. The two cannot be equal; they cannot be in the same state. For example, a slave whose owners are many, differing and quarrelling among themselves, and another slave who belongs to only one serious master.

Lesson No. 218: Explanation of the Verses

Verse No. 21

This scene to which the Qur'an draws our attention here is one that is repeated everywhere on this earth. So much so that the wonder within this scene is lost through repetition, and man becomes familiar with it. The Qur'an presents these very scenes again for deep reflection, so that man may consider the development of this scene step by step. Look: water is descending from the heavens. What is this water, and how is it coming? Since it keeps descending, we pass over it as though it were nothing. This water and its creation are in themselves a miracle. Although we have come to know only this much, that it is a precise combination of two atoms of hydrogen with one atom of oxygen, our knowledge is still only this: Allah created hydrogen and oxygen in the universe and then brought about conditions in which these atoms joined together, and as a result of this union water came into being. After this, the existence of life on this earth was made possible, and the hand of Allah's power lies behind all these matters. All these things are the craftsmanship of Allah the Exalted. Then the sending down of this water from the heavens, in this particular manner, is another miracle: that the earth and this universe were made in such a way that the falling of waters became possible. Then the stage that follows is that:

﴿فَسَلَكَهُ يَنَابِيعَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ (39:21) "Then He makes it flow as springs in the earth." This includes the rivers that flow upon the earth, and the reservoirs that move beneath the surface of the earth and emerge in the form of springs and fountains. Or wells are dug into the earth's surface and the water is made to flow, in such a way that Allah keeps this water close to the surface, and these waters do not go so deep that they can never return.

﴿ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعًا مُخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَانُهُ﴾ (39:21) "Then by it He brings forth crops of varying colours." The plant life that emerges as a result of rain, and is produced by rain, is a miracle that human effort cannot match. A tiny shoot that pushes its head out of the earth, tears apart the heavy weight of the soil, lifts its head into the open air, breathes, enjoys light and wind, and sways freely in the open atmosphere, and then gradually rises up into the air. The mere observation of this tiny shoot fills the human heart and mind with the remembrance of Allah, and it stirs within a human being a wave of awareness of Allah the Creator of the universe, who gave every thing its existence and then guided it. Then, in a single plot of land, various kinds of fruits, not merely different fruits but even a small plant, indeed even a small flower, is a great exhibition-hall of the power of Allah the Exalted. Man, by analysing a single flower alone, expresses his own helplessness. Then this green crop, having finished its greenness, ripens and, having completed its days,

﴿ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَاهُ مُصْفَرًّا﴾ (39:21) "Then it dries up, and you see it turn yellow." The crops ripen and dry, and then you see that they have turned yellow. And they reach the end that has been decreed for them in the natural law of this universe, and having passed through the stages of life, they ripen.

﴿ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطَامًا﴾ (39:21) "Then He makes it crumble into chaff." Its appointed time arrives. It fulfils its role, and its term, which Allah the Giver of Life set for it, comes to an end.

﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ (39:21) "Indeed in that is a reminder for people of understanding." Those of understanding who reflect, take a lesson, and make use of the faculties and the intellect that Allah has given them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verses 22–23:

Verses 22 to 23

Just as rain descends from the heavens, plants grow from the earth and their colours differ, so too from the heavens descends remembrance and admonition. Living hearts benefit from this remembrance; the doors of those hearts are open. They take guidance and advance towards good deeds. And just as the rain of the heavens does not produce crops on stones, so too the remembrance of the heavenly message has no effect on hard-hearted people, and no growth of goodness arises in them, nor the growth of good thought.

Allah opens the hearts of those for Islam in whom He knows there is good. The light of Divine guidance reaches them, and they shine forth, and light blossoms from them. The difference between hearts that have been opened and hearts that are hard is very great.

﴿Woe, then, to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah﴾ (39:22): ﴿those are in manifest error﴾ (39:22). This verse describes the condition of hearts that open to Islam, who take guidance from Islam, receive freshness from Islam, and connect their hearts to Allah. From the state of their opened breasts arise their freshness, the cheerfulness and joy found within them, and the states of radiance and illumination. In contrast, this verse also describes the condition of hearts that are hard and like stone, which have died because of their dryness, have become barren and dark. In short, Allah opens the heart of whomever He chooses for Islam, and the light of Islam enters their hearts; and whomever He wishes to deprive, He hardens his heart. And there is a very great difference between the two.

The second verse explains how the people of faith receive the Noble Qur'an. The Qur'an is a Book in which there is no contradiction. In its nature and temperament, in its direction, its spirit and its characteristics, it is similar and repeated (mutashabih wa mathani) from all these angles. Its concluding parts of verses (the maqta'), its narratives, its instructions and its scenes are repeated again and again, yet there is no contradiction in them. Each time they are repeated from a new angle, each time they seem new, and each time they yield a new benefit, in perfect harmony, perfect seriousness, and in accordance with firm principles, in which there is neither clash nor conflict. Those who fear their Lord, who abstain in accordance with His commands, who live their lives in constant caution, and who are always hopeful of Allah's bounty, receive the rain of mercy of the Qur'an with great awe and trembling. They are so deeply affected that they tremble, the hairs of their bodies stand on end, and afterwards a state of tranquillity settles upon their souls, their hearts become familiar with this remembrance, and then their hearts soften and accept this admonition. This is a living, sensitive situation. This situation is adorned with the colour of words, and these images appear as though they were alive and moving.

﴿That is the guidance of Allah; He guides with it whomever He wills﴾ (39:23). These hearts do not tremble on their own; rather, they are between the two fingers of the All-Merciful, and by the grace and bounty of the All-Merciful they respond, and light comes into being within them. Allah has knowledge of the reality of all hearts. Therefore He guides some and lets others go astray, but this is in accordance with the disposition of those hearts.

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ (39:23). Allah leaves such a person astray because that person chooses error, and Allah knows that he has done so or will do so, and that he will never accept guidance nor bow his head before it.

Verse 24

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verses 25–26:

Verses 25–26

This is the state of those who deny, in both this world and the Hereafter. In this world too, Allah humiliated and disgraced them. In the Hereafter too, a great punishment awaits them. The Sunnah of Allah (the established way of Allah) takes its course. It is unchanging. The fate of past nations is not hidden. He is a witness, a just witness. Verses 27 to 29

Allah sets forth a parable of a servant who is a monotheist (muwahhid) and a servant who is a polytheist (mushrik). Their case is like that of a slave who belongs exclusively to one master, and another who is jointly owned by several partners of differing minds. Verse 33

Here the details of the God-fearing (muttaqin) and of the reward prepared for them are given.

This is a comprehensive way of expression: whatever the heart of the believer finds desirable, and whatever longing arises in his heart, will be prepared for him by his Lord. It will be his right, in which there is no loss, and no part of it will be wasted.

﴿That is the recompense of the doers of good﴾ (39:34). And this is so that what Allah had willed for them of goodness and honour becomes a reality, and so that He deals with them beyond justice, in grace and generosity.

Verse 35

This is because justice would require that both good deeds and evil deeds be taken into account, and that both be requited with reward and punishment... But here Allah will show grace and bounty. Allah will cast the radiance of His mercy upon His God-fearing servants, such that He will erase their very bad deeds. Therefore, they will have no reckoning in the balance, and He will also give them their reward in the best manner, that is, beyond their due. Accordingly, their good deeds will be given extra weight in their scales. This is Allah's grace, and it is His will to bestow it upon whomever He wishes. Indeed, Allah has made this promise to His servants who fear Him, so it will certainly come to pass, and the people of taqwa (God-consciousness) are content with it.

Lesson No. 220 — Overview

This surah's journey is longer and broader than all the other journeys in it. It treats the doctrine of Tawhid (Divine Oneness) from various angles and gives very subtle arguments for it, and these arguments are extremely varied. The lesson opens with the inner state of a true believer who relies solely on Allah, regards Allah alone as the great power, and pays no heed to any weak and insignificant powers apart from Him. Therefore he severs ties with all those powers, leaves the decision regarding his affairs and theirs to the Day of Judgment, and continues on his path with steadfastness, confidence and certainty.

After this, the duty of the Messenger ﷺ is defined, and it is said that you are not responsible for them or their guardian, that you must necessarily bring them onto the path of guidance. That is in Allah's power: their forelock is in Allah's hand, in every state and every circumstance. For people there is no intercessor besides Allah; the authority of intercession rests with Allah. He is the owner of the heavens and the earth, and everyone will return to Him.

Then the polytheists are mentioned, and their psychological condition is that when the word of Tawhid is mentioned, their disposition becomes constricted, and when they hear a word of shirk, they become very pleased. After this the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is commanded to proclaim the word of Tawhid and to leave the polytheists to Allah. A picture of them is placed before you: on the Day of Resurrection they will wish to ransom themselves by giving the wealth of the whole earth and as much again. This is because there they will see the kingdom of Allah, by which they will be dumbfounded.

Their condition is that when they fall into some calamity, they call upon Allah alone, but if they attain prosperity, they become arrogant and begin making lofty claims. Some of them even say that this wealth has been given to us because of our knowledge and technology. This is the same statement that people before them made, and Allah seized them, and they could not become an obstacle before Allah, nor could they overpower Him. As for the expansion and constriction of provision, it is dependent upon the sunan (laws) of Allah, and these laws of Allah's power operate in accordance with His wisdom. He is the One who grants abundance in provision, and He is the One who constricts the provision of whoever He wills.

إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ (39:54) "Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe."

Lesson No. 220 — Explanation of the Verses

Verses 36 to 40. These four verses show what the straightforward, simple reasoning of the believers is like, how natural and forceful this reasoning is, and how clear and deep it is. Just as this reasoning and thinking is in the mind of the Prophet ﷺ, so too it should be in the heart of every believer, whose faith in the Messenger ﷺ is firm, who stands upon this same call, who conveys it, who regards it as his constitution and charter, and for whom it is sufficient and healing.

Narrations regarding the revelation of this verse state that the polytheists of Makkah used to frighten the Messenger ﷺ with their idols and their wrath, while the Messenger ﷺ used to set before them these attributes of theirs and describe their helplessness and powerlessness. The polytheists of Makkah would frighten the Messenger ﷺ that if he did not remain silent about their idols, these idols would harm him.

However, the meaning of this verse is broader than that particular occasion of revelation. Its scope is every call to truth that rises on this earth for the establishment of the Islamic order, and every power that opposes that order and that call, because here the complete reliance, tranquillity and certainty of the believers who raise the call of truth is mentioned, and the opposing powers are also weighed correctly to see what their weight is.

﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ (39:36). Yes, Allah is sufficient. So who are those people by whom the Messenger ﷺ is being frightened? When Allah is with His servant, what is the status of other creatures, especially when he has taken the station of the Messenger and is also fulfilling the right of servanthood? Allah is All-Powerful and controls all His servants.

﴿And they frighten you with those other than Him﴾ (39:36). How can the Messenger ﷺ be frightened? How can all other powers besides Allah frighten the one whom Allah protects? All the powers on the face of the earth are inferior to Allah.

This is a completely simple and clear matter. It requires no great debate, dispute, or much deliberation. The supporter of the Prophet ﷺ and of every caller is Allah, and all other powers are inferior. When a person takes this position, there remains no doubt or ambiguity that the will of Allah alone is enforced and the wish of Allah alone prevails. He decides among His servants: regarding their persons, regarding their hearts, and regarding their thinking and consciousness as well.

﴿Whomever Allah sends astray, there is none to guide him, and whomever He guides, there is none to mislead him﴾ (39:36-37). Allah knows who deserves misguidance, so He lets him go astray; and He knows who deserves guidance, so He guides him. Whatever decision He makes about anyone, there is no one who can change His decision.

﴿Is not Allah Almighty, Owner of Retribution?﴾ (39:37). Yes, He is the Owner of Retribution, the Mighty and Powerful, and He gives all people their due recompense according to their deserts. Whomever He takes retribution from, he truly deserves it. Therefore the one who worships Him has no fear of anything; He is sufficient and the Guardian.

After this, by reasoning according to their own logic and their own point of view, the same conclusions are drawn, and they acknowledged this logic and this way of thinking, and they held this kind of conception of Allah.

﴿And if you ask them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they will surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered: if Allah intends some harm for me, can those you invoke besides Allah remove His harm? Or if He intends mercy for me, can they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; in Him rely those who rely."﴾ (39:38). When these people were asked who the Creator of the heavens and the earth is, they would acknowledge that the Creator of the heavens and the earth is Allah alone. No person of sound nature can give any other answer, and no intelligent person can name any other cause of the creation of the heavens and the earth than the Exalted and Lofty Being. Therefore the Qur'an turns them, and all rational people, to this fact: that it is seated within your nature and is very clear. If that is the case, then who is there who can stop the affliction which that Exalted Being wishes to bring upon His servants, or who in the heavens and the earth can stop His mercy if He wishes to show mercy to someone?

The definitive answer to these questions is "No." If this matter is settled, then from whom can the caller to Allah fear, of whom be apprehensive, and in whom place his hopes? Who can remove his calamities? Who can keep Allah's mercy away from him? Who can disturb him, frighten him with threats, and turn him from his path? When this belief settles in the heart of the believer, the matter concerning him is ended, the dispute is ended, and all hopes in other than Allah are ended. Only hope in Allah remains. He is sufficient for His servants, and we should place our trust in Him alone.

﴿Say, "Allah is sufficient for me, and in Him rely those who rely."﴾ (39:38). After this it is said that you should announce that you have complete trust, reliance and certainty in the Lord, the Exalted. Such trust in which there is no doubt, such certainty in which there is no wavering, and such tranquillity in which there is no trace of restlessness. With this provision you should set out and not rest until you reach the destination.

﴿Say, "O my people, act according to your standing, indeed I am acting; so you will come to know who will receive a humiliating punishment and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment"﴾ (39:39-40). Tell them plainly: "O my people, carry on with your work in your place, I will carry on with my work; you will come to know upon whom will come a humiliating punishment, and who will receive the punishment that never ends." In other words, you act according to your own method, and I have set out on my own path, neither fearing nor having any doubt. You will soon come to know that in this very world a punishment that brings disgrace will come upon you, and then in the Hereafter this punishment will be everlasting.

This matter has been decided, and it was decided through the natural reasoning to which every sound-natured person bears witness, and to which this whole universe bears witness, that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the Creator of the earth. The call which all the Messengers have presented until today is the call of Allah. Therefore, for the Messengers of Allah and the callers to truth, who in the heavens and the earth possesses any authority? Is there anyone who can remove their afflictions? If this is not so, why do people fear other than Allah and these worldly powers? The truth is that the matter is clear, the path is plain, and there is now no further need for debate.

This is the relationship of the Messengers and the callers to truth with those powers which try to block their way. Now the question is: what is the duty of the Messengers and the callers in regard to the call of truth, and how will they conduct themselves towards those who deny?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verses 41–44:

Verses 41 to 44

"Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book for mankind in truth" (39:41). The nature of this Book is truth. The way of life and the system of existence that it grants to human beings is true. Its law is true, and this is the truth by which the heavens and the earth are sustained. The order that this Book has laid down for human beings and the code that Allah has laid down for the running of this universe are both true, and they are harmonious and in agreement with one another. This truth has been sent down for the people, so that they may take guidance from it and live their lives in accordance with it, and you are the one who conveys this truth. And it is for them to decide whether they choose the path of guidance or the path of misguidance, whether they obtain the blessings of Paradise or choose the fire of Hell. Every person may lead his own self wherever he wishes. You are neither responsible for them nor their guardian.

"Whoever follows guidance does so for his own benefit, and whoever goes astray bears the consequence of his straying alone. You are not responsible for them" (39:41). Their responsibility rests with Allah. They are in the power of Allah while awake and also while asleep, and in all their conditions they are in His power, and He directs them within as He wills.

"It is Allah who takes the souls at the time of death, and those who have not yet died He takes during their sleep. Then He keeps back those upon whom He has decreed death, and sends the others back until a specified term" (39:42). Allah takes the souls of all the dead at their appointed times. Before that, Allah also takes the soul of every person during sleep, even though that person is not dead. Yet at that time too the soul is taken, for a fixed term. If the appointed term arrives while the person is asleep, he does not wake up again. If the appointed term has not yet come, the soul is sent back and the person wakes up. Therefore all souls are in the power of Allah, both in sleep and in waking.

"Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect" (39:42). In short, these people are in the power of Allah, Allah alone is responsible for them, and you are not responsible for their final outcome. If they attain guidance, they attain it for themselves, and if they adopt the path of error, they do so to their own detriment. Accountability is for all, and no one will be left unaccounted for. Lesson No. 221: Explanation of the Verses

Verse No. 53

The mercy of Allah is so vast that it can envelop the greatest disobedience, whatever it may be. This is a general call to repentance and return. It is an invitation to those who have gone very far on the paths of misguidance, immorality, and wickedness, and have become hopeless. They are invited not to despair of the mercy of Allah, to place their trust in Allah, for the door of Allah's mercy is wide and the mantle of forgiveness and pardon is very open. He is merciful and generous to His servants. He knows how weak and frail His servants are. He knows that their conduct is influenced by internal and external factors. Allah also knows that the accursed Satan lies in ambush and sits on their paths from every side, right and left, and misguides them. He has launched all his cavalry and infantry against humankind, and he is very serious in his wicked plan. And Allah knows that the structure of man is very weak, and as soon as this wretched one's hand loses the firm rope, he inclines toward evil through his personal inclinations, carnal tendencies, and psychological tendencies, his balance is lost, he takes the paths of deviation, and having lost his balance, he sets out on the paths of disobedience.

Allah is aware of all these weaknesses of His creation. Therefore Allah helps him, extends the skirt of His mercy for him, and gives punishment only when all means have been used for his reform so that he may come onto the right path, and when he has gone far away on the paths of disobedience, has exceeded limits in sins, and becomes certain that he is rejected and repudiated, and that for him there is now neither return possible nor forgiveness, in such a state of despair and hopelessness he hears this call of Allah:

﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (39: 53).

This person has exceeded limits in disobedience, has drowned in sins, has fled from a safe place, and has strayed from the path. Now, between him and the shade of mercy, the refreshing mercy, the life-giving mercy, the gentle and tender mercy, there remains only one door. This is the door of repentance. This door is always open; there is no gatekeeper upon it. To reach the shades of the mercy of Allah through this door, no permit is needed; simply repent and return, "Return a hundred times, repent, and come back."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 39, verses 54–55:

Verses 54 to 55

Repentance (inabah), Islam, and returning within the sphere of submission and surrender carry one and the same meaning and are one and the same reality. Entering into the fold of obedience to Allah is an act in which there are no formalities, no obstacles, and no intermediary or intercession. Whoever wishes, at whatever time he wishes, may enter the simple system of Islam.

Islam is a religion of direct connection between the servant and the Lord. It is a direct relationship between the Creator and the created. Whoever among the sinners wishes to turn back, and whoever among the misguided wishes to return, and whoever has disobeyed to whatever extent, let them surrender and come back; the door is open. A shady refuge exists. A fresh, gentle and tender atmosphere exists. And all these things are within a door that has no gatekeeper, and for entering through this door there is no reckoning or accounting.

Return, return, before a voice comes saying: "So-and-so, you are not [to be] helped!"

Min qabli ... tubsiroon (39:54): "Before the punishment comes upon you, and then you cannot be helped from anywhere." There will be no helper there. So come, for there is no delay in the end of time. At any moment the decision of the final hour may come and the door may be closed. At any time of the night or day, the moments of respite may end.

Wa-ittabi'u ... Rabbikum (39:55): "And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord." This refers to the Qur'an, which is in your hands.

Min qabli ... la tash'uroon (39:55): "Before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive it." Therefore, turn back before the opportunity is lost, before the respite is gone, and you have fallen short regarding the right of Allah, and then you regret, saying: "Why did we mock the promise of Allah?"

Abandon your extravagance, abandon deviation, and give up immorality and transgression, before the punishment of Allah comes upon you while you have no awareness of it.

This is the final outcome: there is a group whose faces are black with shame. Moreover, with grief, and because of the flames of Hell. These are the people who considered themselves very great upon the earth. They were called to the worship of Allah by night and by day. This call remained in place even when they were submerged in sins up to their necks, but they paid no heed to the call of the caller. Today this group is very ashamed. Their faces are black from shame and dejection, while the other party has been saved and has succeeded. Now there remains no possibility of any harm reaching them, nor will they face any anxiety. This is the party of certainty, who lived in the world in such a way that they feared the Hereafter and remained hopeful of the mercy of Allah. Today they are in salvation, success, peace and security.

Lesson No. 222: At a Glance

This is the final lesson of this surah. It takes up the theme of the reality of Tawhid (Divine Oneness) in relation to the creation of the universe: that Allah has created all things, and that He has absolute dominion over all things. Therefore, the proposal of the polytheists that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) should worship their deities and that they, in return, would worship the Lord of the Worlds, so that a common religion would come into being, is an extremely foolish and bizarre proposal and demand. Allah is the Creator of the universe. All authority and sovereignty over the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone. He has no partner. How is it possible that something else should be worshipped alongside Him, when the keys of the heavens and the earth are in His hand? That is the reality.

﴿وَمَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾ "They have not appraised Allah with the appraisal due to Him." These people associate others with Allah, whereas Allah alone is the worthy of worship, the Possessor of power, and the One who controls the whole universe.

﴿وَالْأَرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾ (39:67) "On the Day of Resurrection the whole earth will be in His grip, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand." To record this reality in this manner, one scene from the scenes of the Resurrection is presented, and this scene concludes with the angels circling the Throne of Allah barefoot, glorifying Him along with His praise. The entire universe will be engaged in praising Him, and it will be said, from every direction and every side: ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ "All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds." And this will be the decision in the reality of this universe.

Lesson No. 222: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 62 to 63

This is the reality to which everything bears witness. No one can claim to have created anything, and no sensible person can claim that this universe came into existence on its own without any Creator. Indeed, every existing thing within this universe, both its essence and its design, shows that it has been made with purpose. Nothing appears to be by chance, whether small or great.

﴿وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ﴾ (39:62) "And He is Guardian over all things." He is the One who runs the heavens and the earth, and He runs them according to His will and purpose. This whole universe moves according to Allah's system of decree and destiny. No will other than Allah's will has any part in these affairs. Nature bears witness to this, the reality of events confirms it, and human reason and conscience also testify to it.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾ (39:63) "And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, it is they who are the losers." They are deprived of the knowledge and awareness through which their lives would remain in harmony with the movement of this entire universe. This is a great loss for them. They are deprived of the comfort of guidance and the beauty of faith, and they are also deprived of the sweetness of the certainty and tranquility of belief and conviction. In the Hereafter they too will be losers, and their families will be losers because of them. Their loss is so great that the word "losers" (al-Khasirun) applies to them.

In light of this reality, to which the heavens and the earth bear witness, and to which every thing in this universe bears witness, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is instructed to say to them: What do you propose? That I should worship your deities, and in return you worship the Lord of all the Worlds? How utterly ignorant is this proposal! Is truth a commodity that is bought and sold in the marketplace?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verse 64:

Verse 64

This is a natural rebuke, and the appropriate answer to the baseless proposal of these people is evident from the very proposal itself, namely how deeply immersed in ignorance they were and how utterly blind they were. Then, after this, the polytheists are warned, and the first addressee of this warning is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and all the prophets (peace be upon them). Regarding the prophets, the concept of shirk cannot even be imagined. In reality, this warning is directed at their nations, that they should not associate anyone with the Being of Allah, should worship none but Allah, and that all human beings, including the prophets (peace be upon them), should regard Allah as One without partner.

The warning against shirk is concluded with a command to remain steadfast in tawhid (the affirmation of Allah's oneness). That is: worship Allah alone, and give thanks to Allah for faith and guidance, and give thanks for the blessings of Allah which envelop His servants and which they cannot even count, while they are immersed in them:

Verse 66

Now the discussion turns to the power of Allah, glory be to Him, and to the station of Allah, with which they were proposing to associate partners.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 39, verse 67:

Verse 67

The truth is that they did not give Allah His due regard. Otherwise, they would not have associated with Him His creation. Nor have they rendered Allah the worship that is His right, because they could not comprehend the belief in Tawhid (Oneness of Allah) and Allah's greatness. They have no awareness of Allah's majesty and exalted status. The awareness of Allah's majesty and greatness is given to them in the manner of the Qur'an's distinctive style of expression: the Qur'an presents even lofty rational ideas in a highly concrete form, so that universal and rational meanings come close to limited human perception.

Wherever such images and scenes appear in the Qur'an and Sunnah, they are in fact parables (tamthilat), and an attempt is made to bring realities closer to human perception. The purpose is to express meanings in words whose imagining is possible for them. Here too, the absolute power of Allah has been brought in the form of a fist; otherwise, He is not bound by any form, any place, or any limit. Here rational truths have been given a sensory form. After this comes a long scene of the Day of Resurrection. It begins with the first blast of the Trumpet (nafkhah ula) and ends when all the affairs of the Resurrection have been settled, the people of Hell have been driven toward Hell, and the people of Paradise have been sent off toward Paradise, and only the Divine Being remains, while the entire universe is glorifying and praising the Divine Being.

This is a tremendous scene, full of fervour and movement, and its motions begin gently and in good order and advance until all movements end, all sounds fall silent, and a terrifying stillness settles over the scene. All creatures are struck with awe before Allah, the One, the Irresistible.

Behold! A harsh sound rises, and all people die and fall. At that moment the entire population on earth becomes lifeless in the twinkling of an eye. The entire creation of the heavens also perishes, except those whom Allah wills (illa ma sha'Allah). Now we do not know after how long a pause the second blast will sound. But the second blast does sound.

Verse 68

Here the third sound is not mentioned, the one in which there will be a gathering and a summons to appear before Allah. Nor is the outcry of the resurrection and the din of the crowd depicted, because the aim is to present this scene in an extremely calm and tranquil manner.

And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord (39:69). That is, the field on which the Resurrection will take place; it will be a place illuminated by the light of the Lord, with no other light.

And the Book will be placed (39:69): the book in which the record of people's deeds will be written.

And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought (39:69), so that they may speak the truth which they knew, and every dispute will be settled there, in utmost silence, because in this scene all matters are decided with humility and submission. No dispute will remain.

There is no need here for anyone to speak, nor any need to raise a voice. Thus the reckoning of all of humanity is wound up in great silence and in summary, whereas in other scenes details are given, because the purpose here is to show that on that Day the awe and fear of Allah will prevail. Before the majesty of Allah, no one will have the strength to draw a breath.

Verse 71

Here the angels will receive them and say: Yes, you deserve this Hellfire, and these are its causes. The decree of Allah against the disbelievers has been issued with truth, and there is no doubt about it. So the disbelievers here, without any further dispute, accept it, acknowledge that they were guilty, and submit.

Verse 72

This is the caravan of the people of Hell, the caravan of the arrogant. They have gone, and their gates were opened for them... But look, on the other side the caravan of the God-conscious (muttaqeen) is also approaching. This is the caravan of the people of Paradise!

Verse 73

This is an excellent welcome. It is a praise, and within it the reason for it is also stated: ﴿Tibtum﴾ "You are well", that is, you remained pure. You were pure. You came in purity, because in Paradise there will be only pure people. Only pure people can enter there, for there is eternity and blessings. Now here the voices of the people of Paradise rise with utmost humility, and they glorify and extol Allah in soft voices.

Verse 74

They have inherited the land of Paradise. They go wherever they wish within it and settle wherever they like. They eat whatever they desire; everything is available. Now this scene concludes in an extremely awe-inspiring manner, yet this majesty too is of a very gentle kind. In harmony with the atmosphere of this scene, the whole universe is glorifying its Lord, and it does so in a very quiet manner, with humility and reverence, and every living creature repeats its words with utmost submissiveness.
